text: Bitcoin jumped another leg higher today, touching levels last seen in January, but a big part of today's move came from mechanics, not fresh conviction: roughly $650 million in short positions got force-liquidated over the past day, and traders betting against Bitcoin were essentially squeezed into buying it back at higher prices. That squeeze pushed Bitcoin above its 50-week moving average for the first time in 45 weeks, a technical level chart-watchers treat as a genuine trend shift rather than just a bounce. It's happening alongside real tailwinds too: oil prices have eased back under $100 a barrel and Treasury yields have softened, both of which take pressure off risk assets generally. Spot Bitcoin ETFs are also pulling in fresh money again after a quiet patch, and corporate buyers haven't stopped either, with Strategy and Strive both adding tens of millions of dollars worth of coins this week. The catch is that short squeezes tend to run hot and then give some of it back once the forced buying dries up, so don't be surprised if part of today's gain fades once the mechanical part of the rally is done. Even after this surge Bitcoin is still more than 30% below its record high near $126,000, so this reads as a genuine recovery rally rather than a fresh all-time-high push. Put together, the trend looks constructive into the rest of the week, but today's speed was amplified by short covering rather than pure demand, so a bit of give-back before the next leg up wouldn't be surprising, and none of this is financial advice.
